tools.name: Frying pan (about 24 cm)
tools.note: Handles everything from frying to simmering.

tools.name: Wooden spatula or cooking chopsticks
tools.note: For stirring the bottom while it simmers.

tools.name: Measuring cup
tools.note: A 500 ml bottle filled to about 80% works too.

tools.name: Lid
tools.note: For an extra steam if the rice is still chalky at the end.

steps.title: Cut bacon
points: Cut the bacon into strips about 1 cm wide.
This is the only knife work in the recipe.

steps.title: Fry bacon
points: Put the strips in a dry frying pan.
Cook over medium heat for about a minute.
The fat that renders out becomes your cooking oil.

steps.title: Add rice
points: Tip in the rice as it comes, unwashed.
Stir for a minute, until every grain is coated in fat.
Stop when the rice turns faintly translucent.
steps.hint: Rinsing washes off the surface starch, and with it the creaminess. For risotto, unwashed is correct.

steps.title: Add water and bouillon
points: Pour in 400 ml of water and drop in the bouillon cube.
Break the cube up with the spatula as you stir.
Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil.

steps.title: Simmer rice
points: Drop to low heat once it boils.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Stir slowly from the bottom about every 3 minutes.
steps.hint: Skip the stirring and the bottom scorches. Keep the heat low and stay close to the stove.

steps.title: Check rice
points: Crush a grain of rice and taste it.
Still chalky in the center: add 50 ml of water and simmer 3 minutes more.
Soupy: raise to medium heat for about a minute to drive off the excess.

steps.title: Add cheese and butter
points: Kill the heat first.
Add the 2 tablespoons of grated cheese and 10 g of butter, and stir for about 20 seconds.
Season with salt and black pepper.
steps.hint: Add cheese over a live flame and it splits, leaving a grainy texture.

troubleshooting.solution: The heat was too high. Drop it to the lowest setting and stir every 2 minutes instead. Don't stir the burnt layer in. Scoop only from the top when serving.
Not enough water. Add 50 ml at a time and check every 3 minutes. A lid speeds things up, but traps moisture, so take it off and reduce for a final minute.
Raise to medium heat and reduce for about a minute while stirring. It tightens a little from residual heat after plating, so stop while it's just slightly loose.
A scant teaspoon of salt plus a teaspoon of mentsuyu (if you have it) stands in. The bacon brings salt too, so hold back and adjust by taste at the end.
Two sausages or a can of tuna works instead. For tuna, add it oil and all, and halve the butter.
